text:
Both responses identify the same core problems: the concurrent-duplicate race, the non-durable in-memory Set, the non-constant-time signature comparison, missing error handling, the missing amount check, and replay protection. Both lead with the race, which is the most important issue given the stated duplicate behavior.

Response B is somewhat better. It adds the crash-between-side-effect-and-mark issue, a real failure mode that Response A doesn't name directly. Its fixes are precise, such as a unique constraint written in the same transaction as the invoice update, and it notes that `timingSafeEqual` throws on mismatched lengths. Its amount-check item explains the consequence (underpayment marked paid). It is also closer to the 200-word limit and has no preamble.

Response A has some strengths. Its race fix (claim before processing, release on failure) is a good concrete pattern, and it distinguishes 400 from 500 responses, which is useful for retry behavior. However, its opening sentence is filler, and it runs noticeably longer without adding much more correct substance.

Verdict: B
